#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""End-to-end link check: arms, servos, servo-load sensing, and cameras.

Read-only. Keeps motor torque DISABLED throughout, so the arms stay limp and
nothing moves. Run it with both arms powered and both cameras connected:

    python3 ~/tactilevla-verify.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import cv2
from lerobot.motors import Motor, MotorNormMode
from lerobot.motors.feetech import FeetechMotorsBus

# Ports come from ~/tactilevla-ports.json so a macOS renumbering is one command
# (`python3 ~/tactilevla-findports.py --write`) instead of a six-file edit.
PORTS_JSON = Path.home() / "tactilevla-ports.json"
if not PORTS_JSON.exists():
    sys.exit(
        f"Missing {PORTS_JSON}\n"
        "  Plug in both arms (power bricks first), then:\n"
        "    python3 ~/tactilevla-findports.py --write"
    )
_ports = json.loads(PORTS_JSON.read_text())
FOLLOWER_PORT = _ports["follower"]["port"]
LEADER_PORT = _ports["leader"]["port"]

# Present_Voltage is in units of 0.1 V and is the ONLY thing that distinguishes
# the two arms electrically - they have identical motor IDs (1-6), so connecting
# to the wrong port succeeds and reads six healthy servos. Asserting the band
# turns "the operator eyeballed the number" into a hard gate, which is what
# catches a leader/follower cable swap.
VOLTAGE_BANDS = {"FOLLOWER": (100, 140), "LEADER": (40, 60)}  # 12 V brick / 5 V brick

# Camera roles, indices and resolutions come from one shared file so a macOS
# renumbering is a one-line fix instead of six. See ~/tactilevla-cams.json.
CAMS_JSON = Path.home() / "tactilevla-cams.json"
_cams = json.loads(CAMS_JSON.read_text())
TOP_CAM = _cams["top"]["index"]
WRIST_CAM = _cams["wrist"]["index"]
RECORD_RES = {
    role: (
        tuple(int(v) for v in os.environ[f"{role.upper()}_RES"].split("x"))
        if f"{role.upper()}_RES" in os.environ
        else (_cams[role]["width"], _cams[role]["height"])
    )
    for role in ("top", "wrist")
}

JOINTS = ("shoulder_pan", "shoulder_lift", "elbow_flex", "wrist_flex", "wrist_roll", "gripper")

# STS3215 Max_Temperature_Limit defaults to 70 C. Stay well under it.
TEMP_WARN_C = 50
TEMP_STOP_C = 60


def build_bus(port: str) -> FeetechMotorsBus:
    motors = {name: Motor(i + 1, "sts3215", MotorNormMode.DEGREES) for i, name in enumerate(JOINTS)}
    motors["gripper"] = Motor(6, "sts3215", MotorNormMode.RANGE_0_100)
    return FeetechMotorsBus(port=port, motors=motors)


def check_arm(label: str, port: str) -> bool:
    print(f"\n--- {label} @ {port} ---")
    bus = build_bus(port)
    try:
        bus.connect(handshake=False)
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"  FAIL connect: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
        return False

    ok = True
    try:
        bus.disable_torque()  # keep the arm limp for a pure read

        try:
            positions = bus.sync_read("Present_Position", normalize=False)
            print(f"  positions : {[f'{k}={v}' for k, v in positions.items()]}")
        except Exception as exc:
            print(f"  FAIL reading Present_Position: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
            ok = False

        # Temperature matters for long recording sessions: STS3215s throttle and
        # eventually fault when hot, and a 140-episode session is long enough to
        # get there. Feetech's own Max_Temperature_Limit default is 70 C.
        try:
            temps = bus.sync_read("Present_Temperature", normalize=False)
            hottest = max(temps.values())
            if hottest >= TEMP_STOP_C:
                note = f"  <- TOO HOT (>={TEMP_STOP_C} C), stop and let it cool"
            elif hottest >= TEMP_WARN_C:
                note = f"  <- warm (>={TEMP_WARN_C} C), take a break soon"
            else:
                note = ""
            print(f"  Present_Temp (C) : {dict(temps)}  max={hottest}{note}")
            if hottest >= TEMP_STOP_C:
                ok = False
        except Exception as exc:
            print(f"  WARN reading Present_Temperature: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")

        # This is the signal the tactile plan depends on.
        for register in ("Present_Load", "Present_Current", "Present_Voltage"):
            try:
                values = bus.sync_read(register, normalize=False)
                print(f"  {register:16s}: {dict(values)}")
                if register == "Present_Voltage":
                    lo, hi = VOLTAGE_BANDS[label]
                    volts = max(values.values())
                    if not lo <= volts <= hi:
                        other = "LEADER" if label == "FOLLOWER" else "FOLLOWER"
                        o_lo, o_hi = VOLTAGE_BANDS[other]
                        print(
                            f"  FAIL: {label} should read {lo}-{hi} "
                            f"({lo / 10:.0f} V brick) but reads {volts} ({volts / 10:.1f} V)."
                        )
                        if o_lo <= volts <= o_hi:
                            print(
                                f"        That is the {other}'s voltage - the two arms are "
                                "SWAPPED.\n"
                                "        Fix with: python3 ~/tactilevla-findports.py --write"
                            )
                        else:
                            print("        Check the power brick and the barrel connector.")
                        ok = False
            except Exception as exc:
                print(f"  FAIL reading {register}: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
                if register == "Present_Load":
                    ok = False
    finally:
        with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
            bus.disconnect()
    return ok


def check_camera(label: str, index: int) -> bool:
    cap = cv2.VideoCapture(index)
    if not cap.isOpened():
        print(f"  FAIL {label} (index {index}): could not open")
        return False
    # Open at the resolution that will actually be RECORDED (see
    # ~/tactilevla-record.sh), not 1080p. Checking a camera at a resolution you
    # never record with tells you nothing about the recording.
    width_req, height_req = RECORD_RES[label]
    cap.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_FOURCC, cv2.VideoWriter_fourcc(*"MJPG"))
    cap.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_WIDTH, width_req)
    cap.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_HEIGHT, height_req)
    for _ in range(5):
        cap.read()
    good, frame = cap.read()
    width = int(cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_WIDTH))
    height = int(cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_HEIGHT))
    cap.release()
    if not good:
        print(f"  FAIL {label} (index {index}): opened but no frame")
        return False
    gray = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
    brightest = int(gray.max())
    focus = float(cv2.Laplacian(gray, cv2.CV_64F).var())
    size_note = "" if (width, height) == (width_req, height_req) else "  <- NOT the requested size"
    verdict = "OK" if brightest >= 20 else "DARK - lens blocked?"
    print(
        f"  {label:6s} idx={index}  {width}x{height}  bright_max={brightest:3d}  "
        f"focus={focus:6.0f}  {verdict}{size_note}"
    )
    # focus is Laplacian variance, which measures how much EDGE DETAIL is in view.
    # It is not comparable between cameras: an overhead camera aimed at a blank
    # white table scores low no matter how sharp it is, while a wrist camera
    # filled with the textured gripper scores high. So it is reported, never
    # asserted on. Compare a camera only against ITSELF on the same scene - that
    # is what makes it useful for confirming a refocus actually helped.
    return brightest >= 20 and (width, height) == (width_req, height_req)


def main() -> int:
    print("=" * 62)
    print("TactileVLA-Edge link check (read-only, torque stays disabled)")
    print("=" * 62)

    follower_ok = check_arm("FOLLOWER", FOLLOWER_PORT)
    leader_ok = check_arm("LEADER", LEADER_PORT)

    print("\n--- CAMERAS ---")
    top_ok = check_camera("top", TOP_CAM)
    wrist_ok = check_camera("wrist", WRIST_CAM)

    print("\n" + "=" * 62)
    results = {
        "follower arm": follower_ok,
        "leader arm": leader_ok,
        "top camera": top_ok,
        "wrist camera": wrist_ok,
    }
    for name, passed in results.items():
        print(f"  {'PASS' if passed else 'FAIL'}  {name}")
    print("=" * 62)

    if all(results.values()):
        # The one thing this script CANNOT check. Both cameras support 640x480
        # and 800x600, so opening index 1 at 800x600 succeeds whichever camera is
        # physically on index 1 - a swapped pair passes every automated check
        # here. Only a human looking at the two windows can settle it, and
        # recording a session with the roles reversed is unrecoverable.
        print("\nElectrically linked. ONE CHECK LEFT, and it cannot be automated:\n")
        print("    python3 ~/tactilevla-camview.py")
        print("\n  The window labelled 'top' must show the TABLE FROM ABOVE.")
        print("  The window labelled 'wrist' must show the GRIPPER.")
        print("  If they are swapped, edit ~/tactilevla-cams.json and swap the two")
        print("  'index' values, then re-run this. Do NOT judge by focus score.")
        return 0
    print("\nSomething is not linked - see failures above.")
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Tests for the overhead-camera realignment math in tactilevla-camalign.py.

The tool's job is to say how far the live view has drifted from a saved reference, so
these feed it a synthetic textured scene with a KNOWN shift, rotation or zoom and check
that the estimate comes back within a pixel or so.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
from pathlib import Path

import cv2
import numpy as np

TOOL = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "software" / "tools" / "tactilevla-camalign.py"
_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("camalign", TOOL)
assert _spec is not None and _spec.loader is not None
camalign = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec)
_spec.loader.exec_module(camalign)

W, H = 960, 540


def scene(seed: int = 0) -> np.ndarray:
    """A grayscale scene with plenty of edges and texture to align on."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    img = np.full((H, W), 90, np.uint8)
    for _ in range(400):
        x, y = int(rng.integers(0, W)), int(rng.integers(0, H))
        w, h = int(rng.integers(8, 60)), int(rng.integers(8, 60))
        cv2.rectangle(img, (x, y), (x + w, y + h), int(rng.integers(0, 256)), -1)
    return img


def warp(img: np.ndarray, matrix: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    return cv2.warpAffine(img, matrix, (W, H), borderMode=cv2.BORDER_REFLECT)


def test_identical_views_are_aligned() -> None:
    ref = scene()
    transform = camalign.estimate_transform(ref, ref.copy())
    assert transform is not None
    m = camalign.misalignment(transform, W, H)
    assert m["max_err"] < 1.0
    assert camalign.status(m["max_err"]) == "ALIGNED"


def test_translation_is_measured_with_sign() -> None:
    ref = scene()
    # Content in the live view sits 12 px right of and 7 px above the reference.
    live = warp(ref, np.float32([[1, 0, 12], [0, 1, -7]]))
    m = camalign.misalignment(camalign.estimate_transform(ref, live), W, H)
    assert abs(m["dx"] - 12) < 1.0
    assert abs(m["dy"] - -7) < 1.0
    assert abs(m["rotation_deg"]) < 0.2
    assert camalign.status(m["max_err"]) == "MOVE"


def test_rotation_is_measured_with_sign() -> None:
    ref = scene()
    # OpenCV's positive angle turns the image counter-clockwise on screen.
    live = warp(ref, cv2.getRotationMatrix2D((W / 2, H / 2), 3.0, 1.0))
    m = camalign.misalignment(camalign.estimate_transform(ref, live), W, H)
    assert abs(m["rotation_deg"] - 3.0) < 0.2
    assert abs(m["dx"]) < 1.0 and abs(m["dy"]) < 1.0


def test_zoom_is_measured() -> None:
    ref = scene()
    live = warp(ref, cv2.getRotationMatrix2D((W / 2, H / 2), 0.0, 1.04))
    m = camalign.misalignment(camalign.estimate_transform(ref, live), W, H)
    assert abs(m["scale_pct"] - 4.0) < 0.3


def test_small_drift_reads_close_not_aligned() -> None:
    ref = scene()
    live = warp(ref, np.float32([[1, 0, 6], [0, 1, 0]]))
    m = camalign.misalignment(camalign.estimate_transform(ref, live), W, H)
    assert camalign.status(m["max_err"]) == "CLOSE"


def test_unrelated_scene_returns_none() -> None:
    blank = np.full((H, W), 128, np.uint8)
    assert camalign.estimate_transform(scene(), blank) is None


def rearrange_workspace(img: np.ndarray, box: tuple[int, int, int, int]) -> np.ndarray:
    """Replace a region with different content: the arm and objects moved."""
    x, y, w, h = box
    out = img.copy()
    out[y : y + h, x : x + w] = scene(seed=99)[y : y + h, x : x + w]
    return out


WORKSPACE = (240, 100, 480, 340)  # the middle of the frame, where the arm works


def test_moved_objects_in_excluded_area_do_not_count() -> None:
    ref = scene()
    live = rearrange_workspace(ref, WORKSPACE)
    mask = camalign.static_mask(W, H, [list(WORKSPACE)])
    m = camalign.misalignment(camalign.estimate_transform(ref, live, mask), W, H)
    assert camalign.status(m["max_err"]) == "ALIGNED"


def test_camera_shift_is_measured_while_objects_move() -> None:
    ref = scene()
    live = rearrange_workspace(warp(ref, np.float32([[1, 0, 10], [0, 1, 4]])), WORKSPACE)
    mask = camalign.static_mask(W, H, [list(WORKSPACE)])
    m = camalign.misalignment(camalign.estimate_transform(ref, live, mask), W, H)
    assert abs(m["dx"] - 10) < 1.0
    assert abs(m["dy"] - 4) < 1.0


def test_static_mask_scales_boxes_to_a_smaller_image() -> None:
    # Boxes are stored in full-resolution pixels; matching runs at half size here.
    mask = camalign.static_mask(W // 2, H // 2, [[200, 100, 400, 200]], factor=2.0)
    assert mask[75, 200] == 0  # inside the box (full-res 400, 150)
    assert mask[10, 10] == 255  # static area


def test_different_scene_is_not_matched_to_a_wrong_answer() -> None:
    # A camera pointed at a different scene must read "no match", not a confident
    # nonsense offset - a wrong number is worse than none when re-aligning by hand.
    assert camalign.estimate_transform(scene(seed=0), scene(seed=5)) is None


def test_box_dragged_past_the_window_edge_still_masks() -> None:
    # A drag that leaves the window can report negative coordinates; the box must be
    # clipped to the image, not silently dropped by an empty slice.
    mask = camalign.static_mask(W, H, [[-5, -10, 40, 50]])
    assert mask[0, 0] == 0
    assert mask[30, 30] == 0
    assert mask[45, 40] == 255


def test_guidance_tells_the_user_to_undo_the_offset() -> None:
    # Content sits right/up of the reference, turned counter-clockwise, too big.
    text = " ".join(
        camalign.guidance(
            {"dx": 12, "dy": -7, "rotation_deg": 1.5, "scale_pct": 2.0, "max_err": 30}
        )
    )
    assert "12 px LEFT" in text and "7 px DOWN" in text
    assert "clockwise" in text and "counter-clockwise" not in text
    assert "raise the camera" in text


def test_full_resolution_frames_are_measured_in_full_resolution_pixels() -> None:
    # The live tool matches on a 960 px copy of 1920 px frames; offsets must come back in
    # full-res pixels, with the moving-area mask scaled to match.
    big = cv2.resize(scene(), (W * 2, H * 2), interpolation=cv2.INTER_NEAREST)
    live = cv2.warpAffine(
        big, np.float32([[1, 0, 30], [0, 1, -14]]), (W * 2, H * 2), borderMode=cv2.BORDER_REFLECT
    )
    workspace = [[480, 200, 960, 680]]
    live[200:880, 480:1440] = 0  # the arm moved through the workspace
    ref_small, factor = camalign.to_gray_small(cv2.cvtColor(big, cv2.COLOR_GRAY2BGR))
    live_small, _ = camalign.to_gray_small(cv2.cvtColor(live, cv2.COLOR_GRAY2BGR))
    mask = camalign.static_mask(ref_small.shape[1], ref_small.shape[0], workspace, factor)
    small_t = camalign.estimate_transform(ref_small, live_small, mask)
    m = camalign.misalignment(camalign.to_full_res(small_t, factor), W * 2, H * 2)
    assert abs(m["dx"] - 30) < 1.0
    assert abs(m["dy"] - -14) < 1.0

"""Documentation integrity checks.

These run in CI to catch dead internal links and malformed ADRs before they reach `main`.
Docs are reviewed in the same PR as the code they describe, so they are held to the same gate.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from pathlib import Path

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent

# Matches [text](target) but not image embeds ![text](target).
MD_LINK = re.compile(r"(?<!!)\[[^\]]+\]\(([^)]+)\)")

REQUIRED_TOP_LEVEL = (
    "README.md",
    "CONTRIBUTING.md",
    "CHANGELOG.md",
    "COMPATIBILITY.md",
    "LICENSE",
    "LICENSE-hardware",
    ".gitignore",
    ".env.example",
)

REQUIRED_DIRS = ("software", "firmware", "hardware", "docs", "tests")


def markdown_files() -> list[Path]:
    return [p for p in REPO_ROOT.rglob("*.md") if ".git" not in p.parts]


def test_required_top_level_files_exist() -> None:
    missing = [name for name in REQUIRED_TOP_LEVEL if not (REPO_ROOT / name).exists()]
    assert not missing, f"missing top-level files: {missing}"


def test_required_directories_exist() -> None:
    missing = [name for name in REQUIRED_DIRS if not (REPO_ROOT / name).is_dir()]
    assert not missing, f"missing directories: {missing}"


def test_internal_markdown_links_resolve() -> None:
    """Every relative markdown link must point at a file that exists."""
    broken: list[str] = []
    for md in markdown_files():
        for target in MD_LINK.findall(md.read_text(encoding="utf-8")):
            if target.startswith(("http://", "https://", "mailto:", "#")):
                continue
            path_part = target.split("#", 1)[0]
            if not path_part:
                continue
            if not (md.parent / path_part).resolve().exists():
                broken.append(f"{md.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)} -> {target}")
    assert not broken, "broken internal links:\n" + "\n".join(broken)


def test_adrs_are_well_formed() -> None:
    """Each ADR needs a status, a date, and the Context/Decision/Consequences sections."""
    adr_dir = REPO_ROOT / "docs" / "adr"
    adrs = sorted(adr_dir.glob("[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-*.md"))
    assert adrs, "no ADRs found"

    problems: list[str] = []
    for adr in adrs:
        text = adr.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        if "**Status:**" not in text:
            problems.append(f"{adr.name}: no Status")
        if "**Date:**" not in text:
            problems.append(f"{adr.name}: no Date")
        for section in ("## Context", "## Decision", "## Consequences"):
            if section not in text:
                problems.append(f"{adr.name}: missing {section}")
    assert not problems, "malformed ADRs:\n" + "\n".join(problems)


def test_adr_numbers_are_unique() -> None:
    adr_dir = REPO_ROOT / "docs" / "adr"
    numbers = [p.name[:4] for p in adr_dir.glob("[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-*.md")]
    assert len(numbers) == len(set(numbers)), f"duplicate ADR numbers: {numbers}"


def test_env_example_has_no_real_secrets() -> None:
    """`.env.example` is a template: keys may be listed, values must be blank or placeholders."""
    lines = (REPO_ROOT / ".env.example").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    suspicious: list[str] = []
    for line in lines:
        line = line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
            continue
        key, _, value = line.partition("=")
        if key.strip().endswith(("TOKEN", "KEY", "SECRET", "PASSWORD")) and value.strip():
            suspicious.append(key.strip())
    assert not suspicious, f"populated secret values in .env.example: {suspicious}"

It never saw B2. It picked the noodle up anyway.

A sub-$300 arm, taught by 160 human demonstrations. Two policies, ACT and SmolVLA, both picked the noodle up from the one spot no demonstration ever touched.

Watch the real runs Read the results

The 3D arm on this page is a reconstruction from the SO-101’s URDF. The real footage is further down.

Six hobby servos and a 3D printer.

The SO-101 is an open-source arm: printed links, six Feetech STS3215 servos, two USB cameras. The published tactile-VLA work runs on research arms that cost around $30,000. This setup costs under $300 — roughly a hundredth.

≈ 1/100the cost of the research arms behind published tactile-VLA work

One arm is driven by hand. The other copies it, and that’s how every demonstration was recorded.

160 demonstrations, one hand at a time.

Every episode is a person driving a leader arm while the follower copies it, then resetting the scene by hand. Eight cells on a 3×3 grid, exactly 20 episodes each, the noodle rotated through ±90° in 10° steps.

Four rounds around the perimeter, the walk order reversed on rounds 2 and 4, so no cell always sits at the same point in a round.

Two cameras. One goes blind at the worst moment.

The overhead camera frames the workspace at 800×600. At the instant of grasp, the gripper hides the object from it — so a 640×480 camera on the wrist keeps the contact legible. That blind spot is the case for touch.

Two policies, the same 160 episodes.

About 52M parameters

  • ResNet18 vision backbone
  • Predicts 100 actions at a time
  • 42,308 training steps
  • Learning rate 1e-5, constant

About 450M parameters

  • Pretrained vision-language model, vision encoder frozen
  • Predicts 50 actions at a time
  • 20,000 training steps
  • Learning rate 1e-4, warmup then decay

Both trained on one RTX 3060. Both run on a MacBook.

The trail follows the reconstruction’s scripted path, sized to each policy’s chunk length (100 vs 50). It illustrates chunking; it is not policy output.

Zero training episodes. Both policies succeeded.

A policy that memorized its training trajectories and one that learned the task can look identical on the cells they trained on. The clean test is to put the object somewhere it has never been. B2 has trained cells on all four sides and none inside, so it tests whether the policy can interpolate.

The servos already report load.

Every STS3215 reports its own load. Pressed by hand on the bench, peaks ran from 48 to 152 by joint. That makes it a candidate touch signal with no added hardware.

It isn’t in either policy yet. The readings come in steps of 4, light contact reads exactly zero, and every value includes pose-dependent static torque, not contact alone. Phase 3 wires it in on a contact-rich insertion task — with a go/no-go on whether touch actually beats vision.
